name: ROGII 14th place: hierarchical 1-D U-Net stack with seed averaging (keithtyser / Keith Tyser)
authors_org: Keith Tyser (Kaggle ktyser / keithtyser), solo; the author says coding agents wrote the code, launched and watched the runs, and drafted the writeup
venue_link: Kaggle writeup https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/rogii-wellbore-geology-prediction/writeups/14th-place-a-hierarchical-u-net-stack-with-seed-a ; training code https://github.com/keithtyser/rogii-wellbore-geology-solution (docs/RECIPE.md, submissions/README.md, features/README.md)
code_availability: Public training code on GitHub (scripts/train_unet.py plus 20 modules in src/rogii_research, fold file folds_random.csv, XGBoost margin and gate scripts, stacking and recipe scorers, all 13 submission recipes, verify_construction_a.py for fold safety). The Kaggle inference notebook runs from frozen checkpoints. [uncertain] Whether the checkpoints/weights are published is not stated in the README, and the license was not checked.
evidence_level: Competition writeup plus code, with a full ledger of all 13 submissions (CV, public, private). Not peer-reviewed. The Kaggle writeup page could not be rendered by the fetcher; details come from the GitHub docs.
extreme_summary: A 1-D U-Net per well with cosine candidate matching and an expected-value decode over 512 candidate depths (0.5 ft, temperature 2.0), trained with synthetic-well pretraining (lineage: 26th place, Tucker Arrants). Stacked hierarchically: 30-checkpoint blend -> per-well hard gate vs an XGBoost margin model -> width-96 minus width-48 'scale direction' -> seed-averaged width-64 direction, each added with a fold-safe coefficient. CV 6.2518, public 6.004, private 6.329 (14/6,125, gold). The unselected simple ridge/simplex blends scored better privately (6.266).
task_definition: Predict blind-zone TVT for every row of each horizontal well from GR, trajectory, typewell and the known prefix; scored by pooled row RMSE.
inputs: Horizontal GR (including a long GR window of 51), trajectory with inclination trig features, typewell (candidate curve matching), a 32-column history (known prefix) and a 640-column future; 96 temporal context channels. The XGBoost margin model uses 143 features in the absolute field frame (trajectory, 'Q3D', six-path and typewell stencil). The gate uses 1,250 target-free well aggregates.
target_parameterisation: Classification over 512 candidate TVT rows at 0.5 ft (a 256 ft window) around the anchor, with auxiliary regression and slope targets. The structural identity TVT + Z - ANCC = const per well (from the discussion board, holding to ~0.03 ft) is credited in the README. [uncertain] Exactly how that identity enters the features was not verified in code.
output_representation: Per-column (block of 16 rows) categorical distribution over 512 candidate depths; point estimate by mean decode. Final submission is a linear combination of member point predictions.
architecture: 1-D encoder-decoder U-Net over the well log at widths 32 (tctx96 bank), 48, 64 and 96, block size 16, dropout 0.25, plus a cosine trajectory refiner head and multi-head cosine candidate matching against the typewell. Four-level stack: (1) base = 30-checkpoint U-Net blend (fixed weights 0.608/0.222/0.169 over three sub-banks) and an XGBoost model predicting a margin on that blend; (2) GateV2 = hard per-well choice between them from 1,250 target-free well features; (3) add c_fold * (pred_w96 - pred_w48) at block 16 (raw width-96 alone was worse and rejected twice); (4) add c_fold * (mean of 16 width-64 checkpoints over 4 seeds - gated base), with c between 0.34 and 0.52 per fold.
core_mechanism: Variance reduction and bias correction by fold-safe, shrunk residual stacking. Each stage adds a 'direction' (difference between a stronger/averaged model and the current base) scaled by one coefficient fitted on the other four folds. Seed averaging matters because single runs are very noisy: two runs with the same seed and config on different GPUs differed by up to 34.5 ft on single rows (residual correlation 0.857), the same spread as between different seeds. The XGBoost works only as a margin on the incumbent (6.34 vs 15.93 when predicting raw TVT).
training_objective: Classification 1.0 (soft target, sigma 1.0) + regression 0.10 (Cauchy, scale 1.5) + slope 0.10 + history supervision 0.25 (sigma 0.75) + candidate curve prior logit 0.75 (sigma 10.0), prior sigma 3.0. 60 epochs with 10 pretrain epochs, batch 1, 4 samples per well, AdamW-style lr 3e-4, wd 1e-4, clip 1.0, patience 12, cosine annealing with T_max = epochs (the author warns that changing epochs changes the schedule shape). Synthetic augmentation: synthetic probability 0.50, flip 0.25, path noise 6.0, GR noise 1.0.
decoding: Mean (expected value) over 512 candidates with decode temperature 2.0 (softens the softmax before the expectation); MC dropout samples 1. Then linear stacking.
metric_consistent_decode: Yes. Mean decode, pooled RMSE objective, linear blends fitted on RMSE. The temperature-2.0 softening is a calibration knob that pushes toward the Bayes-optimal mean under an over-confident posterior. [uncertain] Whether T = 2.0 was tuned or inherited is not documented.
evidence_scope: Whole lateral (640 future columns + 32 history columns) against the typewell; single well only (the XGBoost features are in an absolute field frame but no explicit neighbour-well evidence is described).
prefix_conditioning: Known prefix enters as 32 history columns with its own supervision loss (weight 0.25). No test-time fine-tuning.
propose_vs_select: Both. Blends and 'direction' additions are proposals averaged linearly; GateV2 is a hard per-well selection between two bases (hard gate 6.3358 vs soft blend 6.3412 vs 198-feature gate 6.3418: tiny differences).
physical_constraints: Candidate curve prior logit (sigma 10) and slope loss encourage plausible paths; the structural identity is acknowledged; no hard layer-ordering or continuity constraint in the decode.
dataset: ROGII Kaggle: 773 training wells, 3,783,989 scored rows, fixed 5-fold whole-well random split (folds_random.csv, never changed after week one), plus synthetic wells at probability 0.5.
synthetic_to_real: Synthetic-well pretraining (10 pretrain epochs) then mixed training with synthetic probability 0.5, synthetic flip 0.25, path noise 6.0, GR noise scale 1.0; recipe credited to the 26th place public work (Tucker Arrants). No separate real-only alignment stage is described.
metric_and_performance: All pooled RMSE. Submitted Construction A: CV 6.2518 / public 6.004 / private 6.329 (14/6,125). d96 scale stack: 6.3174 / 6.102 / 6.341. ABS-frame XGB margin: 6.3429 / 6.094 / 6.306. 30-checkpoint blend: 6.4052 / 6.110 / 6.313. Sum-to-one ridge (penalties 10 -> 0.01): CV 6.455-6.548, private 6.283 -> 6.266. 9-member simplex: CV 6.5648, private 6.266. Early best-CV single U-Net: 6.6846 / 6.258 / 6.485. Per-fold CV of the final model: 6.59, 6.61, 5.90, 6.64, 5.43. Main takeaways: seed/checkpoint averaging moved a single U-Net from 6.685 to about 6.40 CV (-0.28), and 6.485 to about 6.27-6.31 private (-0.18 to -0.22). The later stacking stages gained 0.15 CV but nothing privately (6.313 -> 6.329).
comparability: Moderate for relative effects, weak for absolutes. Same competition data and metric family (pooled RMSE), but 5-fold CV over all 773 wells vs our fixed 155-well holdout, and the model family is a 1-D U-Net (not the 1st-place 2D cost-image ConvNeXt). The relative gains (seed averaging ~0.2-0.3 ft; stacking ~0 private) should transfer as a rough guide.
validation_protocol: Fixed 5-fold whole-well random split (not spatially/pad grouped); every weight, coefficient, penalty and gate fitted on 4 folds and applied to the 5th, checked by verify_construction_a.py (fold-safe refit within 0.033 of frozen coefficients; a leaky same-fold refit would score 6.207). CV-to-private gap: CV ordering did not predict private ordering. The best CV (6.2518) scored 6.329, while worse-CV ridge/simplex blends scored 6.266, a warning that complex stacking fits fold noise.
inference_budget: Inference from frozen checkpoints fits the Kaggle notebook limit. [uncertain] Per-well time was not reported. Training: ~3 h per run on an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, ~7 h on a 3090, ~5 GB GPU memory; 16 width-64 runs plus the width-32 bank and width-48/96 pairs.
repeated_layers: Not addressed specifically. Implicitly through the soft classification over candidates with a curve-prior logit, multi-head cosine matching, and averaging many checkpoints, which averages across band choices (softer posteriors closer to the mean decode).
drift: Slope loss (0.10) and the cosine trajectory refiner head target path shape; averaging seeds reduces per-run random drift. No explicit dip state or drift correction.
uncertainty_and_calibration: No calibration analysis reported. Decode temperature 2.0 is a de facto calibration choice (softening). Their seed-reproducibility measurement (residual correlation 0.857 between identical-config runs) is a useful estimate of run-to-run variance.
where_to_use: (a) Seed/checkpoint averaging of our ConvNeXt teacher (and FastViT student) by averaging per-column probabilities before the expectation decode, and distilling FastViT from the seed-averaged teacher posterior. (b) A decode-temperature sweep before the expectation, i.e. a calibration fix. (c) Fold-safe sum-to-one ridge or simplex blending of ConvNeXt/FastViT/AnchorCNN instead of learned per-point gates. (d) The 'margin on incumbent' GBM idea as a residual corrector (low expected value).
error_mode_targeted: Blend/calibration part of band confusion (~15% blend + some wrong_mode through softer, better-calibrated posteriors) and run-to-run variance; also the measurement/protocol noise floor (seed variance).
gap_vs_our_implementation: Confirms our recipe family: expected-value decode over a depth axis, synthetic pretraining, soft classification targets plus a regression auxiliary; independent confirmation that this is what gold looks like. Gaps: (1) We report single models (FastViT 4.84) and one pair (4.69); we do not seed-average. Their data shows single U-Nets are very noisy (identical config reruns correlate 0.857 in residuals, which fits our +-0.39 ft single-run noise floor), and averaging many checkpoints gave -0.2 to -0.3 ft. (2) We do not apply a decode temperature; they used T = 2.0. For pooled RMSE with a mean decode, a softer (better-calibrated) posterior is exactly the 'better calibration' route in our metric analysis. (3) We have not tried fold-safe linear stacking with a shrinkage coefficient. Our learned per-point gates failed; their data say simple ridge/simplex blends beat complex gates on the private set, and hard per-well gates added ~0.007 CV. (4) Their 'width-96 minus width-48' scale direction suggests a cheap multi-capacity difference feature, but it helped only in CV and not privately. (5) Their history supervision loss (weight 0.25) supervises the known prefix explicitly; check whether our cost-image model is supervised on visible columns.
proposed_experiment: E1 (calibration, zero training): in kaggle_1st_place/solution/seq_NN_rescore.py or posterior_analysis.py, apply softmax temperature T in {0.8, 1.0, 1.25, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0} to the dumped logits/posteriors (or p^(1/T) renormalised) before the expectation decode. Fit T on training/OOF wells and report pooled RMSE on the 155 holdout wells for ConvNeXt, FastViT and the pair, with a paired bootstrap against the 4.84 / 4.69 controls. Also report blend/wrong_mode error shares. E2 (seed averaging): train 3 seeds of the best ConvNeXt-small recipe (same config as cnx_mobileone_ep150 or the 60-epoch baseline) and average per-column probabilities (not point predictions) before decoding; compare 1 vs 2 vs 3 seeds to estimate the ensemble curve; control = the existing single seed. E3 (distillation): distill FastViT-SA12 from the seed-averaged teacher posterior versus the single-teacher KD; control = the current 4.84 student. E4 (blending): replace learned gates with a sum-to-one ridge on {ConvNeXt, FastViT, AnchorCNN} point predictions, fitted fold-safe on training-well OOF (or a split of the holdout with cross-fitting), penalty chosen in-fold; control = equal-weight pair 4.69.
implementation_effort: E1 low (post-hoc, minutes). E4 low. E2/E3 medium: no new code, just repeated training runs and a probability-averaging script.
gpu_cost: [uncertain] E1/E4 none. E2: 2 extra ConvNeXt-small training runs on the RTX 5060 8 GB, likely several hours to ~1 day each depending on epochs (their 1-D U-Net took 7 h per run on a 3090 at ~5 GB; our 2D ConvNeXt at 345x400 is heavier). E3: one extra FastViT distillation run. Inference cost scales linearly with the number of seeds for the teacher only; the distilled student keeps single-model cost.
distillation_compatibility: Very good. A seed-averaged teacher posterior is a smoother, better-calibrated KD target (standard ensemble distillation), and the student stays a single FastViT, so rig inference cost is unchanged. The temperature finding transfers directly (KD already uses temperature; decode temperature is separate).
error_correlation_with_ours: Same model family, so members built this way (seeds of our own ConvNeXt) will be highly but not fully correlated. Their measured residual correlation between identical-config reruns is 0.857, which leaves real averaging headroom. A 1-D U-Net member in their style would be more diverse than another ConvNeXt seed, but it is weaker (single model ~6.7 CV on their protocol).
risk: (1) Seed averaging mainly removes variance; it cannot fix systematic wrong-band choices when all seeds share the same bias (~51% band confusion). Oracle best-mode is 4.27, and averaging moves toward the ensemble posterior, not the oracle. (2) Their complex stacking gave CV gains that did not transfer (private got worse), so do not over-engineer per-well gates or scale directions; our own learned gates already failed. (3) Temperature may already be implicitly near-optimal if our training loss (smoothed target + Huber on expectation) calibrates well; the gain may sit below the +-0.39 ft noise floor. (4) GPU time on an 8 GB laptop makes 3+ ConvNeXt seeds expensive; memory might force smaller batch sizes that change the recipe. (5) Their split is random whole-well, not pad-grouped, so their absolute CV may be optimistic.
notes: Lineage: the U-Net-per-well treatment, synthetic-well pretraining and expected-value decode come from the 26th place public work (Tucker Arrants, 'stacked U-Net synthetic wells' writeup), so this is a third independent confirmation of the family our 1st-place reproduction belongs to. Useful facts: the scheduler T_max = epochs couples epoch count to anneal shape (relevant to our 60 vs 150 epoch comparisons); runs are not bit-reproducible across GPUs; margin-on-incumbent beats raw prediction for GBMs by a huge factor (6.34 vs 15.93). The author finished 80th public -> 14th private. Private best 6.266 came from unselected simple blends, which argues for simple fold-safe blending in our setting too.
